title: Tech Note: 4DAF Video Player
author: Joe Resuello, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note walks through embedding 4D Ajax Framework (4DAF) UI objects — an ImageMatrix, a DataFiller, and an IFrame — into a custom HTML page to build a video-browsing front end backed by a 4D database, explicitly warning that as a subscription-based, fast-iterating product the note could become outdated quickly. That caveat proved prescient: 4D Web 2.0 Pack and the 4D Ajax Framework were discontinued long ago, replaced first by other web UI approaches and eventually by 4D's modern built-in Web Server and Qodly component-based tooling, so essentially none of the concrete setup steps or client library calls described here still apply.
related_updates: 4D Web 2.0 Pack and the 4D Ajax Framework (4DAF) have been discontinued and are no longer part of the current 4D product line
Modern 4D web UI development uses 4D's built-in Web Server plus Qodly Studio/Qodly components rather than 4DAF-specific client libraries
The daxipedia.4d.com wiki referenced in the note is no longer a current resource
